subject: Councilor George Scarpelli Re-election Platform
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford City Councilor George Scarpelli regarding his re-election campaign, highlighting his positions on zoning, tax overrides, municipal finances, and proposed charter changes.

items.title: Introduction and Guest Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced the program and welcomed guest Councilor George Scarpelli, who shared his personal, teaching, and coaching background.

items.title: Council Re-Election and Slate Voting
items.summary: Scarpelli discussed his run for re-election to the City Council, advocating for independent candidates to ensure diverse resident representation.

items.title: Zoning Initiatives and Public Process
items.summary: Scarpelli explained his opposition to current neighborhood zoning proposals, arguing they threaten single-family neighborhoods and lack sufficient public input.

items.title: Opposition to Tax Overrides
items.summary: Scarpelli detailed his objections to the recent tax overrides, suggesting that Medford's free cash reserves should have been utilized to level-fund schools instead.

items.title: Revenue Growth, New High School, and Infrastructure
items.summary: Scarpelli proposed generating new city revenue through smart growth in commercial corridors and addressed the need for school and fire department facility upgrades.

items.title: City Council Meeting Structure and Public Podiums
items.summary: Scarpelli criticized the council's decision to meet bi-weekly and called for improved public engagement and respect at the podium.

items.title: Charter Review and Ward Representation
items.summary: Scarpelli expressed strong support for the proposed charter reform to transition the City Council to a ward and precinct representation model.

items.title: Community Activities, Campaign Contact, and Closing
items.summary: Scarpelli shared his favorite aspects of the Medford community and his campaign contact details before Petrella closed the program with community announcements.
